findings.title: Linux: a directory removed and recreated within one 100 ms batch keeps a dead inotify watch, and activation does not restore it
findings.fix: Drop the `!p.exists()` condition and forget `p` and its children on every Remove/rename event. If `p` exists again, `dir && !self.work.contains_key(p)` triggers a walk that re-adds the watch, and the next `set` re-adds pruned git dirs. Add a test that does `remove_dir_all(&d); create_dir(&d)` inside one `t.after`.

findings.title: Linux: `set` re-reads the excludes for the filter but never walks again, so a directory taken out of `info/exclude` stays unwatched
findings.body:
`set` now rebuilds `Current` on every call, so the event filter uses the new `info/exclude` and global excludes. `inner.walk()` still runs only when the root moved. On Linux the per-directory inotify watches come from `files::walker`, an `ignore` WalkBuilder that honors `info/exclude` and `core.excludesFile`. A directory that was excluded at the last walk therefore has no watch.

Failure:
1. `build/` is listed in `.git/info/exclude`.
2. The user removes that line and activates the window.
3. Activation's `set` updates the filter, but no walk runs.
4. Edits under `build/` produce no events and mark nothing, until an unrelated new directory, a `.gitignore` change or a switch of the current repo triggers a walk.

This breaks the goal's "an `info/exclude` change is honored by the next activation" and §7's claim that the walk reruns when an ignore file changes. Three comments overclaim it: `set`'s doc, `activated`'s doc ("reads the excludes again") and the Done note. `the_excludes_are_read_again_on_each_set` tests only the excluding direction, which the filter handles alone. macOS and Windows are not affected.

One reviewer also notes, as pre-existing, that an inotify `Q_OVERFLOW` loses the Create events of directories made during the burst, and `dropped` requests no walk to recover them.
findings.fix: On Linux, walk in `set` when the rebuilt excludes differ from the previous `Current` (or on every activation's `set`). Add the un-exclude direction to the test.

findings.title: The dropped-events test bypasses `Inner::mark`, so nothing checks that an inotify overflow (a Rescan with no paths) marks every repo
findings.body:
inotify's `Q_OVERFLOW` arrives from notify as an `Other` event with the Rescan flag and no paths. Only the new branch in `Inner::mark` (lines 171-177) maps empty `e.paths` to `[PathBuf::new()]`, which means everything.

The test passes `PathBuf::new()` to `dropped` directly and never goes through `Inner::mark`. If that branch regressed, every Linux overflow would mark nothing and the test would still pass.
findings.fix: Have the test also call `t.w.0.mark(vec![Ok(Event::new(EventKind::Other).set_flag(Flag::Rescan))])` and assert that every repo is marked.

findings.title: §7 and TECHDEBT still say activation refreshes every status and every unwatched worktree, but it now skips statuses loaded within 30 s
findings.body: `activated` now calls `pass(cx, false)`, which skips a repo whose status loaded less than 30 s ago. The spec and TECHDEBT still treat activation as the catch-all refresh: §7's table ("the rescan and every status, as today"), §7's over-cap bullet ("refreshes on window activation, as every worktree does today"), and the Step 8 test list ("still refreshes on activation"). TECHDEBT's row says edits "show on activation only" and Windows loses events "until the next activation". None of these hold within 30 s of a repo's last load. The Done note's line 927 ("which refreshes it, is unchanged") is qualified by its very next bullet, which states the 30 s rule, so the outdated text is mainly §7 and TECHDEBT. This is the documentation side of bugs+impl-1: fixing the code there makes these passages true again.
findings.fix: Preferably fix the code as in bugs+impl-1 (skip only where a worktree watch covers the repo), which makes §7 and TECHDEBT true again. Otherwise reword §7's activation row, the over-cap bullet and the TECHDEBT row: a status older than 30 s reloads on activation, and Refresh always reloads.

findings.title: Activation skips statuses loaded in the last 30 s, including repos whose changes no watch can see
findings.fix: Apply the freshness skip only to repos whose worktree the watcher actually covers: the current repo when it has a worktree watch. Every other repo should reload on activation as before. Alternatively, drop the skip.

immaterial.title: `dropped`'s doc comment and the Done note each describe a different half of what it marks
immaterial.body:
The code marks a repo when `p.starts_with(d) || d.starts_with(p)`, which covers both a repo containing `p` and a repo under `p`. The test asserts both directions.
- The doc comment says "what lies there or above it is stale", which leaves out repos under `p`.
- The Done note (PLAN-FOUNDATION.md:907) and the commit summary say "the repos at or under its path". That leaves out the repo containing `p`, which is the common case for a macOS MustScanSubDirs inside a worktree.
immaterial.fix: Say "the repos at, under or above its path" in both places.
